t: Gaza's routed internet holds at a fifth of its pre-war size; no outage alert since September
s: Internet measurements from IODA show Gaza's network stable but deeply shrunk: 155 of 704 pre-war address blocks are visible in global routing. The count edged up from 147 in late September, and IODA has logged no Gaza outage since a 35-minute dip on 16 September.

t: West Bank networks stay steady; two October IODA alerts were measurement gaps, not outages
s: IODA's signals for the West Bank were flat through October. A 30-minute routing blip on 13 October touched 2% of address blocks, and two probing alerts on 15 and 18 October came from a gap that hit Israel, Jordan, Egypt and Lebanon at the same minutes.

t: Ten months after Israel's 4G approval, West Bank phones are still on 3G
s: Israel approved the arrangements for Jawwal and Ooredoo to move to 4G in January, with a rollout expected within months. By August both operators were still preparing, and Ooredoo's own accounts reportedly assume a 2027 start; Gaza was not part of the approval.

t: Israeli forces arrest journalist Saleh Shawka at his home in al-Eizariya
s: Israeli forces arrested journalist Saleh Shawka, a secretariat member of the Democratic Media Forum, at his home in al-Eizariya before dawn on 22 October after searching the house, the forum said, demanding his release.

t: Fibre now carries 71% of Palestinian home internet, but mobile is still 3G and 2G
s: The Palestinian telecom ministry's 2025 indicators show fast growth in home fibre, to more than 327,000 lines. Mobile networks remain stuck on 3G in the West Bank and 2G in Gaza because of Israeli limits on spectrum and equipment, and Gaza's network damage is listed as a reconstruction priority.
p: Ramallah (Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy)

t: Troops enter two Tuqu' classrooms, threaten closure and take Palestinian flags
s: Israeli soldiers walked into two schools in Tuqu', south-east of Bethlehem, during morning lessons, threatened staff and pupils with punishment and closure, and confiscated Palestinian flags. In Bethlehem the same morning, troops reportedly inspected the phone of a student union leader.

t: Journalist Hazem Nasser freed after 27 months held without charge
s: Israel released Tulkarm journalist Hazem Nasser on 20 October after two years and three months of administrative detention, held on secret evidence with no charge or trial, prisoners' groups and local outlets reported.

t: Israeli police arrest 10 after settler attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats
s: Three days after Heidi Levine was beaten, Israeli police arrested 10 people over the weekend's settler attacks on her and on European diplomats in Taybeh. Police did not name the suspects or say what role each played.
p: West Bank (Abu Falah and Taybeh attacks)
n: Heidi Levine Mike Huckabee Maxime Prévot Benjamin Netanyahu

t: Israel tells High Court foreign reporters still cannot enter Gaza without an army escort
s: Answering the Foreign Press Association's renewed request of 27 September, the state told the High Court that journalists must still enter Gaza only with a military escort, citing continuing risks. The court has yet to rule, more than two years after the petition was filed.
p: Supreme Court (High Court of Justice), Jerusalem

t: 7amleh paper traces how Palestinians' phone calls are stored and mined in the cloud
s: A new 7amleh paper argues Israel's interception of Palestinian calls has moved from targeted wiretaps to recording a whole population, made possible by commercial cloud storage. It names Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services and links the system to arrests and self-censorship.
p: West Bank and Gaza; data centres in Europe

t: Asmahan Bkerat's Concrete Land wins London Film Festival's documentary award
s: Concrete Land, the debut feature of Palestinian-Jordanian filmmaker Asmahan Bkerat, won the Grierson Award for best documentary at the BFI London Film Festival. It follows a Bedouin family of Afro-Palestinian origin facing eviction on the edge of Amman.

t: Gaza City buries journalist Obaida Murtaja, reported killed in a drone strike
s: Mourners in Gaza City buried journalist Obaida Murtaja on 17 October after he was killed, local outlets reported, by an Israeli drone strike on a group of people in the al-Nasr neighbourhood. The report has not been confirmed by the syndicate, CPJ or Gaza's media office.
p: Al-Italiani area, al-Nasr neighbourhood, western Gaza City

t: Masked settlers beat Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine during the olive harvest
s: A crowd of masked settlers beat American photojournalist Heidi Levine, working for The Washington Post, in Abu Falah on 16 October while she photographed olive pickers. She suffered broken ribs and vertebrae and a nearly severed finger, and her cameras and phone were stolen.
p: Abu Falah (Khirbet Abu Falah), north-east of Ramallah
n: Heidi Levine Sara Qudah Benjamin Netanyahu

t: CPJ warns of a widening Israeli campaign against Palestinian and foreign journalists
s: The Committee to Protect Journalists demanded that Israel stop a wave of violations against reporters, from the olive-harvest attacks and detentions to the deportation of a Portuguese journalist and entry and visa refusals for foreign correspondents.
n: Sara Qudah Jaafar Ashtiyeh Mohammad Abed Mohammad Atiq Ricardo Esteves Ribeiro Issam al-Rimawi Secunder Kermani Serena Bilanceri

t: Soldiers carry off files and equipment from Addameer's sealed Ramallah office
s: Israeli troops raided the former Ramallah office of Addameer, the prisoners' rights group, loaded its folders, equipment and furniture onto a military trailer and re-posted a closure order. Addameer's former director says the files included prisoners' legal and court records.

t: WhatsApp call rallies settlers to block Palestinian olive pickers near Neve Daniel
s: A "Stop the Harvest" poster circulated in settler WhatsApp groups called on people to gather before dawn near Neve Daniel to stop Palestinian farmers reaching their groves. Footage showed settlers confronting farmers, soldiers and journalists; no response from Meta was reported.
p: Near Neve Daniel, Gush Etzion, south of Jerusalem

t: A year after Saleh al-Jafarawi was shot in Gaza City, his killing remains unexplained
s: Al Jazeera English and supporters marked one year since video journalist Saleh al-Jafarawi was shot dead in Gaza City on 12 October 2025, days after the ceasefire. Accounts of who killed him still differ, and no investigation result was found.

t: Israeli troops hit Palestinian photojournalist Issam al-Rimawi with rubber bullets near Ramallah
s: Israeli troops fired rubber bullets that struck photojournalist Issam al-Rimawi during clashes involving settlers near Ramallah on 10 October, CPJ reported. He said he was wearing a vest marked 'Press'; the army said it used riot-dispersal means.

t: Gaza freelancer Mahmoud Abu Hamda wins Bayeux war-photography prize
s: Gaza-based freelance photographer Mahmoud Abu Hamda won both the jury's photo prize and the public's choice at the Prix Bayeux for war correspondents. AP's Jehad Alshrafi won the young reporter prize and NPR's Anas Baba the radio prize, both for work from Gaza.
n: Mahmoud Abu Hamda Jehad Alshrafi Anas Baba Lyse Doucet Saher Alghorra

t: Man from Deir Samit arrested over video posted on the third anniversary of 7 October
s: Israeli police arrested a man in his twenties from Deir Samit, near Hebron, on suspicion of incitement after he posted a video marking the 7 October attack on its third anniversary. Police say a unit that monitors social media found the post.
n: unnamed man in his 20s from Deir Samit

t: US charity plans AI that listens to Gaza classrooms for "hateful" speech
s: A US charity running schools in Gaza plans to record lessons and use AI to flag speech it considers hateful, antisemitic or inciting. Its own board member and a partner aid group raised objections, and it is not clear whether teachers, pupils or families will be told.

t: UN rapporteur says platforms act as gatekeepers that bury Palestinian voices
s: Francesca Albanese's report to the General Assembly, "Truth under the rubble", says Meta, X and Google decide which Palestinian narratives are seen. It cites near-total compliance with Israeli takedown requests and argues those requests work as removal orders without legal process.

t: Instagram shuts the account holding killed journalist Anas al-Sharif's war archive
s: The Instagram account of Anas al-Sharif, the Al Jazeera correspondent killed in Gaza in August 2025, has been shut down, a statement on his X account said on 9 October. The account held his archive of war reporting; Meta has given no public reason.

t: Syndicate logs 50 violations against journalists in September, many of them arrests
s: The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate recorded 50 Israeli violations against journalists in September: 22 cases of detention or being stopped from working, 11 court appearances and nine arrests. Several journalists were moved into administrative detention without charge.
n: Muath Amarneh Sabri Jibril Alaa al-Rimawi Rasem Obeidat Mohammed Mona Mahmoud Fatafta Rami Nofal Sameh Nazih Darwaza Shadi Hatem Rajai al-Khatib Amid Shehadeh Rabie al-Munir Salwa Abu Libdeh Naqaa Hamed

t: Portuguese journalist arrested at West Bank olive harvest and deported the next day
s: Israeli forces arrested Ricardo Esteves Ribeiro of the Portuguese outlet Fumaça in Rantis on 8 October and deported him on 9 October. He told CPJ he was threatened and blindfolded at a military base after showing his press card.

t: Bayeux memorial adds 56 names of killed journalists, with a tribute to Gaza's reporters
s: Reporters Without Borders unveiled the 2026 stele at the Bayeux Reporters Memorial on 8 October, naming 56 journalists killed doing their work over the past year, with a special tribute to Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza.

t: Bisan Owda marks three years of filming Gaza, months after a brief TikTok ban
s: Gaza journalist and filmmaker Bisan Owda published a video essay on Mondoweiss marking three years of war, describing a population stuck in 2023 and denied time to grieve. In January her 1.4m-follower TikTok account was banned and restored a day later.

t: Three years on, Gaza's media office counts 263 journalists killed and 23 still detained
s: Marking three years of war, Gaza's Government Media Office told Anadolu that 263 journalists and media workers have been killed, 50 detained with 23 still held, and three are missing. The toll rose from 254 to 263 after the October 2025 ceasefire.
n: Ismail al-Thawabta Nidal Suheil al-Wahidi Haitham Jamal Abdul Wahid Ahmad Issam al-Agha

t: Four Palestinian films make Doha Film Festival's 15-title competition
s: The Doha Film Festival, running 19–27 November, has picked four Palestinian films for its international feature competition, including Thirteen in Gaza and Muayad Alayan's Conversation With the Sea. Concrete Land, about a Palestinian Bedouin family in Amman, also competes.
n: Hosam Abu Dan Rabab Khamis Muayad Alayan Mohanad Yaqubi Fatma Hassan Al Remaihi

t: Armed settlers beat AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh at the olive harvest near Aqraba
s: Settlers beat veteran AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh, 58, with rifle butts while he covered attacks on olive pickers near Aqraba, and took his camera gear. A colleague was threatened at gunpoint while soldiers nearby did not step in, AFP said.
n: Jaafar Ashtiyeh John Wessels Phil Chetwynd

t: Israeli forces detain two journalists filming olive-tree uprooting near Jenin
s: Israeli forces detained journalists Mohammed Atiq and Mohammed Abed while they filmed preparations to uproot olive trees in Anza, south of Jenin, and took them away with a group of olive pickers. The syndicate and CPJ both recorded the case.

t: Prisoners' group says Israel now uses "incitement" to police posts, classrooms and posters
s: The Palestinian Prisoners' Society says Israel has turned the "incitement" charge from a case-by-case accusation into a standing system of surveillance over what Palestinians post, teach and display. It points to the arrest of a school principal in al-Eizariya, whose school posters and lessons were presented as evidence.

t: Troops search homes in Kafr ad-Dik and take residents' security-camera footage
s: Israeli forces raided Kafr ad-Dik, west of Salfit, spread through several neighbourhoods, searched homes and seized footage from surveillance cameras, according to local sources quoted by WAFA. No arrests or names were reported.

t: Supreme Court overturns bans on Arab lists before Israel's 27 October election
s: Israel's Supreme Court unanimously struck down the Central Elections Committee's decision to bar the Joint List and Ra'am, and reinstated MK Ofer Cassif by 7–2. Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew after justices signalled his ban would stand.
n: Ofer Cassif Sami Abu Shehadeh David Mintz Alex Stein

t: 7amleh logs 308 violations in three months, most of them incitement left online
s: 7amleh's third-quarter report counts 308 digital violations against Palestinians: 114 cases of censorship of Palestinian content and accounts and 194 cases of violent, inciting or hateful content against them. Instagram and Facebook account for 71% of cases.

t: Drone strike kills Quran Radio presenter in al-Mawasi; Gaza media office count reaches 263
s: An Israeli drone strike killed Mohammed Abdel Aziz al-Najjar, a presenter at Gaza's Quran Radio, while he was preparing a report in al-Mawasi near Khan Younis on 30 September. Gaza's Government Media Office said he was the 263rd journalist killed since October 2023.
p: Al-Mawasi area of al-Qarara, north-west of Khan Younis
n: Mohammed Abdel Aziz al-Najjar Ikrami al-Mudallal

t: Senate votes down West Bank rights report that press groups linked to Abu Akleh
s: The US Senate rejected Senator Van Hollen's resolution requiring a State Department report on West Bank rights abuses and the deaths of nine Americans, by 47 votes to 51, six days after CPJ and others urged support.
n: Chris Van Hollen Tim Kaine Bernie Sanders John Fetterman

t: Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed freed after 13 days in Israeli detention
s: Naqaa Hamed, arrested at an army checkpoint near Bethlehem on 15 September as she returned from a TRT assignment, was released on 28 September. CPJ says she was freed without charge; the journalists' syndicate says on 8,000 shekels' bail.
n: Naqaa Hamed Khaled Mahajnah Sara Qudah

t: CPJ: Israel has killed 247 journalists since October 2023, 189 of them in Gaza
s: In its September appeal on the Shireen Abu Akleh case, CPJ gave its latest count: 247 journalists and media workers killed by Israel since October 2023, including 189 Palestinians killed in Gaza. It says Israeli forces have killed more journalists than any other actor since CPJ began counting in 1992.

t: Prisoners' Society says troops seize and search phones during mass field interrogations
s: The Palestinian Prisoners' Society says Israeli forces held and questioned more than 100 people over two days in al-Mughayyir and Biddu, and that confiscating and searching mobile phones has become a standard part of these on-the-spot interrogations.

t: Thirteen in Gaza, shot entirely in Gaza, wins Toronto's NETPAC award
s: Hosam Abu Dan's debut fiction feature Thirteen in Gaza, made in Gaza with a local cast and crew, won the NETPAC Award at the 51st Toronto International Film Festival. The director could not travel and spoke to the audience by video.
n: Hosam Abu Dan Khalil Al-Muzayyen Mara Matta

t: CPJ and ten groups ask Israel to protect 'NAZA' filmmakers after citizenship threats
s: After ministers threatened to strip Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor of their citizenship over their Venice-prize documentary 'NAZA', CPJ and ten international groups called on Israel to end the campaign against them and guarantee their safety.
n: Yuval Abraham Rachel Szor Miki Zohar Eyal Zamir Benjamin Netanyahu Hagai Matar

t: Prisoners' group: 39 Palestinian journalists in Israeli jails, 21 held without charge
s: The Palestinian Prisoners' Society said the number of journalists in Israeli prisons rose to 39 after Alaa al-Rimawi's arrest on 17 September. Twenty-one are in administrative detention on secret files, and five are women.
n: Alaa al-Rimawi Muath Amarneh Sabri Jibrin Naqaa Hamed Bushra al-Tawil

t: 7amleh report says EU rules give little sight of Palestine-related takedowns
s: 7amleh's "Solidarity Censored" examines how pro-Palestine expression was restricted online in six European countries. It blames a mix of platform policy, national law and government requests, and says the EU's Digital Services Act offers appeal routes but little transparency.
p: France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, UK

t: August report: 84 violations against Palestinian journalists, including a death in custody
s: The syndicate's August tally was 84 violations, led by 30 cases of journalists detained or kept from working. It also recorded seven arrests, six assaults, seven cases of footage confiscated or deleted and one journalist's death in Israeli custody.

t: French court orders Deauville to put back AP photographer's Gaza football picture
s: The Deauville Sport Images Festival swapped Jehad Alshrafi's photo of a football match amid Gaza's ruins for a cycling picture after "pressure". A court in Caen suspended the mayor's removal order as neither necessary nor proportionate.

t: Courts hand light sentences in leaders' speech trials, but Eghbaria's verdict is still awaited
s: Adalah says Israel has moved from prosecuting ordinary Palestinian citizens over posts to prosecuting their political leaders. Two cases ended this summer in far lighter sentences than prosecutors wanted; Raja Eghbaria, convicted over ten Facebook posts, had not been sentenced in any report found.
p: Haifa, Nazareth and Petah Tikva courts
n: Raja Eghbaria Kamal Khatib Mohammad Taher Jabareen Ahmad Khalifa Mohammad Barakeh

t: Internal records show Israel asked Meta to remove Iran-war posts
s: Internal Meta records seen by The Intercept show Israel's government asked Meta to take down posts supporting Iran, mourning Ayatollah Khamenei or showing missile damage, and posts criticising Itamar Ben-Gvir's Al-Aqsa visit. Meta complied in some cases.

t: Study of 3,520 cases finds Meta rarely says which rule Palestinian posts broke
s: A 7amleh and Utrecht University study of 3,520 complaints from 2021 to 2025 finds Meta named a violated rule in only about a third of cases, and in most of those it used its Dangerous Organisations and Individuals policy. For journalists the share was 71%.

t: Joint assessment: four in five of Gaza's telecom assets destroyed, $500m needed to rebuild
s: The final damage assessment by the World Bank, UN and EU puts direct damage to Gaza's telecom sector at US$200.7 million, with 81% of assets destroyed. It estimates US$346 million in sector losses and US$500.5 million needed over five years to rebuild.

t: Israel's Al Jazeera law now reaches websites and YouTube, and runs until end of 2027
s: Israel extended the 2024 "Al Jazeera law" to the end of 2027 and dropped the need for a declared emergency or court approval. In January 2026 it used it to block Al Jazeera's and Al Mayadeen's websites and YouTube channels inside Israel; YouTube complied.
